title: Subregion interaction strength with a GridSearchCV-tuned Random Forest
required_outputs: none named by the instruction; reference writes rf_model_performance.json, rf_test_predictions.csv, subregion_interactions.csv
method: Sum the 5000 OD records to 2139 (Origin, Destination) pairs, attach the six socio-economic attributes of the origin and of the destination (12 features), 80/20 train/test split, GridSearchCV (5-fold, neg MSE) over RandomForestRegressor hyper-parameters, refit best model, report test MSE. Gold: test MSE 5664 (R2 -0.06; mean-only baseline 5348) - the data carry no signal.
benchmark_defects: The data are synthetic and uninformative: FlowVolume is uniform random 1-99 independent of the attributes, so the 'interaction strength' model cannot beat a constant prediction (test R2 ~ 0); the task only tests the pipeline.
No output file is requested; the published reference script only prints the MSE.
'Aggregate the OD flow data to the subregion scale' is ambiguous: the records are already subregion pairs; aggregation means summing duplicate records per pair (2861 duplicates).
checks: required: a captured pair table (2139 or 2095 rows; key columns found by name or by subregion-name values) whose flow column equals the gold pair sums on >= 99 % of pairs
required: origin and destination attributes merged (>= 3 of 6 matched per side, aligned on the key columns or positionally on a captured pair table)

required: an MSE-named value (variable, file, small table wide or long; RMSE squared; train/baseline/cv excluded; ctx.stdout when available) or MSE recomputed from captured test targets/predictions within 0.8-1.5 x variance of aggregated flows; no evidence -> UNVERIFIABLE
required: a captured train/test feature matrix (10-95 % of pairs as rows) contains >= 3 attributes for both origin and destination
required: RandomForestRegressor(...) and GridSearchCV(...) called in the executed code (comments stripped) - the only evidence of the method on this signal-free data
